subject: human teeth
title: What If You Could Grow a Third Set of Teeth? Japan Is Testing a Drug

scenes.text: What if you lost a tooth and simply grew another? A trial in Japan is testing that.
Sharks replace teeth for life. You get two sets. But in 2021, Kyoto researchers found a protein, USAG-1, that acts as a brake on tooth growth.
They built an antibody to block it. In mice, a single dose grew a whole new tooth. Ferrets, whose teeth work like ours, grew a third set.
In October 2024 the first human trial began at Kyoto University Hospital: 30 men aged 30 to 64, each missing at least one molar.
Phase one tested safety, and the company says it passed. Next come children born without teeth. The target for a product is around 2030.
No human has grown a new tooth yet. But the brake pedal has been found.

description:
What if losing a tooth meant growing a new one, like a shark? Researchers at Kyoto University found that a protein called USAG-1 suppresses tooth development; in a 2021 study, an antibody that blocks it grew new teeth in mice and ferrets with a single dose.
In October 2024 the company Toregem Biopharma began a phase one safety trial at Kyoto University Hospital with 30 men aged 30 to 64 missing at least one molar. A trial in children with congenital tooth loss is planned next, with a product targeted for around 2030. So far no human has regrown a tooth.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: About one person in a hundred is born with the wrong number of teeth, which is who the drug is meant for first. Which body part would you most want to regrow?
